title: Surrogate gradients
summary: While learning, pretend the step has a gentle slope. The spikes you see stay sharp.

terms.plain: a pretend slope used only while learning
terms.definition: A smooth stand-in for the missing slope of the spike. It is used on the backward pass and thrown away at test time.

cards.text:
While learning, pretend the step is a gentle hill near the threshold.
A neuron that is close can still get a hint.

The spikes you actually see stay sharp.
The pretend slope is only for the lesson.
When learning is over, it is gone.

question.prompt: When is the surrogate gradient used?
choices: Whenever the neuron spikes for real
question.why: Forward spikes stay all-or-nothing. The stand-in slope is backward only.
question.simpler: If you still see a soft spike at test time, that is a different model.

question.prompt: A wider pretend slope can teach a neuron that never quite reached threshold.
question.why: The hint reaches voltages near the step, not only the single point on it.
question.simpler: Wider is more generous and less exact.

recall.question: Does a surrogate gradient change the spikes you see?
recall.answer: No. It only stands in for the slope while learning.

deeper.note: Section IV-B of the same review is the construction. snnTorch’s default stand-in, if you pass nothing, is the arctangent. fast_sigmoid is the opt-in.

paper.title: Surrogate Gradient Learning in Spiking Neural Networks
